policy: Unmet need means women lack access, information, or agency — not that they want more children.
takeaway_hi: बिहार और झारखंड में गर्भनिरोध की अपूर्ण जरूरत 15% से अधिक है — महिलाएं गर्भधारण रोकना चाहती हैं पर नहीं रोक पातीं।

title: Vasectomy Rate Among Married Men
takeaway: Vasectomy rates are below 1% nationally — India's family planning programme never invested in male methods.
policy: The near-zero vasectomy rate is a policy failure, not a biological inevitability — it reflects gendered programme design.
title_hi: विवाहित पुरुषों में पुरुष नसबंदी दर
takeaway_hi: पुरुष नसबंदी दर राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 1% से नीचे है — भारत के परिवार नियोजन कार्यक्रम ने पुरुष तरीकों में कभी निवेश नहीं किया।

title: Men Who Believe Family Planning Is Women's Re
takeaway: In UP and Rajasthan, 40%+ men believe family planning is women's responsibility.
policy: Men's attitudes toward contraception directly determine women's access; male engagement programmes are critically underfunded.
title_hi: परिवार नियोजन को महिलाओं की जिम्मेदारी मानने वाले पुरुष
takeaway_hi: उत्तर प्रदेश और राजस्थान में 40%+ पुरुष मानते हैं कि परिवार नियोजन महिलाओं की जिम्मेदारी है।

title: Overweight and Obese Women
takeaway: Overweight/obese women exceed 40% in Delhi, Punjab, and Kerala — the nutrition transition is real.
policy: Obesity and undernutrition coexist in the same states — the 'double burden' requires integrated nutrition policy.
title_hi: अधिक वजन और मोटापे वाली महिलाएं
takeaway_hi: दिल्ली, पंजाब और केरल में अधिक वजन/मोटापे वाली महिलाएं 40% से अधिक हैं — पोषण संक्रमण वास्तविक है।

title: Overweight and Obese Men
takeaway: Male obesity follows similar patterns — higher in urban, wealthy, southern states.
policy: Male overweight is rising faster than female in many states; lifestyle disease prevention must target men too.
title_hi: अधिक वजन और मोटापे वाले पुरुष
takeaway_hi: पुरुष मोटापा भी इसी तरह के पैटर्न का अनुसरण करता है — शहरी, संपन्न, दक्षिणी राज्यों में अधिक।

title: Psychiatrist Density per Lakh Population
takeaway: India has 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population — and 80% of them are in 5 states.
policy: Mental health is India's most under-resourced health domain; most districts have zero psychiatric professionals.
takeaway_hi: भारत में प्रति लाख आबादी 0.3 मनोचिकित्सक हैं — और उनमें से 80% केवल 5 राज्यों में हैं।

title: HIV Prevalence Among Adults 15-49
takeaway: HIV prevalence among adults is concentrated in NE states (injection-driven) and southern states (sexually transmitted).
policy: India's HIV epidemic has two distinct geographies requiring two distinct prevention strategies.
takeaway_hi: वयस्कों में एचआईवी प्रसार पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों (इंजेक्शन-जनित) और दक्षिणी राज्यों (यौन-संचारित) में केंद्रित है।

title: Rural consumption per person
takeaway: Rural spending per person runs from ₹2,739 in Chhattisgarh to ₹9,377 in Sikkim, a gap of 3.4 times inside one country.
policy: A single national poverty line converted at one price level treats these as the same economy. State-specific price deflators are not a refinement here, they are the difference between a real estimate and an arithmetic one.
takeaway_hi: ग्रामीण भारत में प्रति व्यक्ति मासिक खर्च छत्तीसगढ़ में ₹2,739 से लेकर सिक्किम में ₹9,377 तक है — एक ही देश के भीतर साढ़े तीन गुना का अंतर।

title: Urban consumption per person
takeaway: Urban spending per person is higher than rural spending in all 36 states and territories. The national gap is ₹6,996 against ₹4,122, about 70 per cent.
policy: Urban-rural is the axis most Indian transfer programmes are least able to see: entitlements are settled at the village or ward, while the gap that drives migration sits between them.
takeaway_hi: सभी 36 राज्यों और केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों में शहरी प्रति व्यक्ति खर्च ग्रामीण खर्च से अधिक है। राष्ट्रीय अंतर लगभग 70 प्रतिशत है।

title: Rural consumption inequality
takeaway: Kerala has the seventh highest rural spending per person of 36 states and territories and the second most unequal rural distribution, at a Gini of 0.255 against 0.237 nationally. A high average is not a flat one.
policy: Ranking states by mean consumption and ranking them by its dispersion produce different lists. Any transfer designed off the mean alone is targeting a state that does not exist.
takeaway_hi: केरल में ग्रामीण खर्च का स्तर भी ऊंचा है और उसका फैलाव भी — गिनी 0.255, राष्ट्रीय 0.237 के मुकाबले।

title: Urban consumption inequality
takeaway: Urban consumption is more unequal than rural consumption in 31 of 36 states and territories. The five exceptions are small island and hill units. Jharkhand has among the lowest urban spending per person and the widest spread.
policy: Cities are where the dispersion is, and where the instruments are weakest: urban India has no counterpart to the rural employment guarantee.
takeaway_hi: लगभग हर राज्य में शहरी उपभोग ग्रामीण उपभोग से अधिक असमान है। झारखंड में शहरी खर्च कम है और फैलाव सबसे अधिक।

title: Female labour force participation
takeaway: Delhi records the lowest female labour force participation in the country at 13.1 per cent, five times below Sikkim's 66.7. Income and participation do not move together across states.
policy: Participation measured on usual status counts unpaid family labour on a farm and does not count housework. Much of the state-to-state range is a measurement boundary, and reading it as a preference is how the number gets misused.
takeaway_hi: दिल्ली में महिला श्रम बल भागीदारी देश में सबसे कम है, 13.1 प्रतिशत — सिक्किम के 66.7 से पाँच गुना कम।

title: Gender gap in literacy
takeaway: Rajasthan's literacy gap is 23.2 percentage points, ten times Kerala's 2.2. The 14 states left grey are not included in the published round.
policy: A literacy gap among people aged 7 and above is an accumulated record, not a current one: it holds decades of school enrolment inside a single number, and closing it has a floor set by how long people live.
takeaway_hi: राजस्थान में साक्षरता का लैंगिक अंतर 23.2 प्रतिशत बिंदु है, केरल के 2.2 से दस गुना अधिक।

title: Child stunting, NFHS-6
takeaway: Between 16.6 per cent in Puducherry and 37.1 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, stunting still differs by more than two times across the country. The India figure fell from 35.5 to 29.3 per cent between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
policy: A national fall hides states that moved the other way. Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep rose, so a programme judged on the India average would miss them.
takeaway_hi: पुडुचेरी में 16.6 प्रतिशत से दादरा और नागर हवेली और दमन और दीव में 37.1 प्रतिशत तक, बौनापन अब भी दो गुना से अधिक अलग है। NFHS-5 से NFHS-6 के बीच भारत का आँकड़ा 35.5 से घटकर 29.3 प्रतिशत हो गया।

title: Institutional births, NFHS-6
takeaway: Nearly every birth now happens in a facility in most states, with Lakshadweep at 100.0 per cent. Nagaland, at 62.2 per cent, is the clear outlier, and India stands at 90.6 per cent, up from 88.6.
policy: When the national figure is near 90 per cent, the remaining gap is concentrated in a few states and in the most remote households, and it needs targeted delivery rather than another national drive.
takeaway_hi: अधिकांश राज्यों में लगभग हर प्रसव अब स्वास्थ्य संस्थान में होता है, लक्षद्वीप में 100.0 प्रतिशत। नागालैंड 62.2 प्रतिशत के साथ स्पष्ट अपवाद है, और भारत का आँकड़ा 88.6 से बढ़कर 90.6 प्रतिशत है।

title: Women who have used the internet, NFHS-6
takeaway: The share of women who have ever used the internet nearly doubled between the two rounds, from 33.3 to 64.3 per cent. It still runs from 48.8 per cent in Tripura to 94.0 per cent in Goa.
policy: Ever having used the internet is a low bar. It says nothing about owning a phone, reading confidently online, or using a service independently, so it should not be read as digital inclusion.
title_hi: इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: दो दौर के बीच कभी इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाओं का हिस्सा लगभग दोगुना होकर 33.3 से 64.3 प्रतिशत हो गया। फिर भी यह त्रिपुरा में 48.8 प्रतिशत से गोवा में 94.0 प्रतिशत तक है।

title: Women with a bank account they use, NFHS-6
takeaway: Access to an account women use themselves has become close to universal. The gap between states shrank to 14 points, from 81.5 per cent in Meghalaya to 95.5 per cent in Ladakh.
policy: An account that a woman uses herself is not the same as control over the money in it. Survey figures on decisions and earnings are the next question to ask.
title_hi: स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले बैंक खाते वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: महिलाओं द्वारा स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले खाते की पहुँच लगभग सार्वभौमिक हो गई है। राज्यों के बीच अंतर घटकर 14 अंक रह गया, मेघालय में 81.5 प्रतिशत से लद्दाख में 95.5 प्रतिशत तक।

title: Spousal violence, NFHS-6
takeaway: Reported spousal violence runs from 1.9 per cent in Ladakh to 36.1 per cent in Bihar. The India figure is 22.3 per cent, down from 29.2 in NFHS-5.
policy: These are what women told interviewers, and a low figure can mean low violence or low willingness to report it. Some state changes between rounds are very large, so read a single state with care.
takeaway_hi: रिपोर्ट की गई पति द्वारा हिंसा लद्दाख में 1.9 प्रतिशत से बिहार में 36.1 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 22.3 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 29.2 था।

title: Women married before 18, NFHS-6
takeaway: Child marriage fell nationally from 23.3 to 20.1 per cent, but it is still 36.4 per cent in West Bengal, more than twelve times the 2.9 per cent of Kerala.
policy: Andaman and Nicobar and Tamil Nadu have no published figure in the fact sheets, so they are grey. A grey state here has no figure, not a low one.
takeaway_hi: बाल विवाह राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 23.3 से घटकर 20.1 प्रतिशत हुआ, पर पश्चिम बंगाल में यह अब भी 36.4 प्रतिशत है, जो केरल के 2.9 प्रतिशत से बारह गुना से अधिक है।

title: Child wasting, NFHS-6
takeaway: Children under 5 who are wasted ranges from 8.1 per cent in Mizoram to 24.2 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The India figure is 19.0 per cent, down from 19.3 in NFHS-5.
policy: Wasting reflects recent shortfalls in food and bouts of illness, so it can move faster than stunting. One survey year is not a trend.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 8.1 से 24.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.0 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 19.3 था।

title: Underweight children, NFHS-6
takeaway: Children under 5 who are underweight ranges from 11.2 per cent in Sikkim to 41.3 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The India figure is 31.8 per cent, down from 32.1 in NFHS-5.
policy: Underweight mixes stunting and wasting, so it is a rougher guide than either measure alone.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 11.2 से 41.3 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 31.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 32.1 था।

title: Exclusive breastfeeding, NFHS-6
takeaway: Exclusive breastfeeding under 6 months ranges from 34.6 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 75.8 per cent in Chhattisgarh. The India figure is 55.8 per cent, down from 63.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: Mothers report this from recall for their youngest child. Small states rest on few cases, and some have no published figure.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 34.6 से 75.8 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 55.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 63.7 था।

title: Full vaccination, NFHS-6
takeaway: Children fully vaccinated, 12-23 months ranges from 64.3 per cent in Nagaland to 93.8 per cent in Goa. The India figure is 82.6 per cent, up from 76.6 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure combines vaccination cards with the mother's recall, and states with few children in this age group give noisy results.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 64.3 से 93.8 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 82.6 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 76.6 था।

title: Caesarean births, NFHS-6
takeaway: Births delivered by caesarean section ranges from 6.4 per cent in Meghalaya to 62.2 per cent in Telangana. The India figure is 27.2 per cent, up from 21.5 in NFHS-5.
policy: There is no single right rate. Whether a rate reflects need or access is a question this survey cannot answer.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 6.4 से 62.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 27.2 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 21.5 था।

title: Women with low BMI, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women with bmi below 18.5 ranges from 3.1 per cent in Andaman and Nicobar to 29.2 per cent in Jharkhand. The India figure is 19.7 per cent, up from 18.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: A BMI below 18.5 marks undernutrition in an adult woman, and it moves slowly between survey rounds.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 3.1 से 29.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.7 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 18.7 था।

title: Overweight women, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women who are overweight or obese ranges from 19.6 per cent in Assam to 51.3 per cent in Puducherry. The India figure is 30.7 per cent, up from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: Overweight now sits beside undernutrition in many states, so one national health message misses both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 19.6 से 51.3 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 30.7 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 24.0 था।

title: High blood sugar in women, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women with high blood sugar ranges from 6.7 per cent in Ladakh to 28.9 per cent in Kerala. The India figure is 17.8 per cent, up from 13.5 in NFHS-5.
policy: These are random blood sugar readings or reported medication, not a diagnosis of diabetes.
title_hi: उच्च रक्त शर्करा वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 6.7 से 28.9 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 17.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 13.5 था।

title: High blood pressure in women, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women with elevated blood pressure ranges from 12.1 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 32.0 per cent in Sikkim. The India figure is 19.4 per cent, down from 21.3 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure includes people already on medicine, so a high share can reflect disease, screening, or both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 12.1 से 32.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.4 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 21.3 था।

title: High blood pressure in men, NFHS-6
takeaway: Men with elevated blood pressure ranges from 14.1 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 36.6 per cent in Kerala. The India figure is 22.1 per cent, down from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure includes people already on medicine, so a high share can reflect disease, screening, or both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 14.1 से 36.6 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 22.1 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 24.0 था।

title: Tobacco use among women, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women who use tobacco ranges from 0.5 per cent in Chandigarh to 61.0 per cent in Mizoram. The India figure is 8.4 per cent, down from 8.9 in NFHS-5.
policy: This is self-reported, and willingness to report differs by state and by sex.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 0.5 से 61.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 8.4 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 8.9 था।

title: Tobacco use among men, NFHS-6
takeaway: Men who use tobacco ranges from 11.4 per cent in Puducherry to 73.6 per cent in Mizoram. The India figure is 36.3 per cent, down from 38.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: This is self-reported, and willingness to report differs by state and by sex.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 11.4 से 73.6 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 36.3 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 38.0 था।

title: Alcohol use among men, NFHS-6
takeaway: Men who drink alcohol ranges from 0.6 per cent in Lakshadweep to 50.5 per cent in Arunachal Pradesh. The India figure is 18.9 per cent, up from 18.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: This is self-reported. State prohibition and local norms shape what men are willing to say.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 0.6 से 50.5 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 18.9 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 18.7 था।

title: Households using iodized salt, NFHS-6
takeaway: Households using iodized salt ranges from 86.5 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 99.9 per cent in Sikkim. The India figure is 94.2 per cent, down from 94.3 in NFHS-5.
policy: A high national share can hide the few states where many households still lack iodized salt.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 86.5 से 99.9 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 94.2 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 94.3 था।

title: Women with their own mobile phone, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women with a mobile phone they use ranges from 47.8 per cent in Chhattisgarh to 91.6 per cent in Sikkim. The India figure is 63.6 per cent, up from 53.9 in NFHS-5.
policy: Having a phone is not the same as having a data connection or using it freely.
title_hi: अपना मोबाइल फ़ोन रखने वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 47.8 से 91.6 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 63.6 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 53.9 था।

title: Women in household decisions, NFHS-6
takeaway: Married women in household decisions ranges from 84.0 per cent in Andhra Pradesh to 98.9 per cent in Nagaland. The India figure is 89.0 per cent, up from 88.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: The measure covers three decisions and only currently married women.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 84.0 से 98.9 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 89.0 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 88.7 था।

title: Teenage motherhood, NFHS-6
takeaway: Girls 15-19 already mothers or pregnant ranges from 0.0 per cent in Chandigarh to 18.0 per cent in Tripura. The India figure is 6.7 per cent, down from 6.8 in NFHS-5.
policy: This is a small share of a small age group, so state figures rest on few cases.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 0.0 से 18.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 6.7 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 6.8 था।

title: Unmet need for family planning, NFHS-6
takeaway: Unmet need for family planning ranges from 4.4 per cent in Andhra Pradesh to 21.0 per cent in Meghalaya. The India figure is 8.5 per cent, down from 9.4 in NFHS-5.
policy: Unmet need is a woman's stated wish to delay or stop childbearing while using no contraception, and it covers currently married women only.
title_hi: परिवार नियोजन की अपूर्ण आवश्यकता, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 4.4 से 21.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 8.5 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 9.4 था।

title: Women with 10 or more years of schooling, NFHS-6
takeaway: Women with 10 or more years of schooling ranges from 32.9 per cent in Tripura to 86.6 per cent in Kerala. The India figure is 46.4 per cent, up from 41.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: Ten years marks the end of secondary school. Years in school are not the same as what was learned.
title_hi: 10 या अधिक वर्ष की स्कूली शिक्षा, महिलाएँ, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 32.9 से 86.6 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 46.4 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 41.0 था।

title: Unemployment rate, PLFS 2025
takeaway: Unemployment rate ranges from 0.9 per cent in Gujarat to 10.0 per cent in Andaman and Nicobar. The India figure is 3.1 per cent.
policy: A low unemployment rate can mean people cannot afford to stay out of work, so it says little about the quality of jobs.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 0.9 से 10.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 3.1 प्रतिशत है।

title: Youth unemployment rate, PLFS 2025
takeaway: Youth unemployment rate ranges from 2.5 per cent in Gujarat to 31.2 per cent in Andaman and Nicobar. The India figure is 9.9 per cent.
policy: Youth rates run well above adult rates, and small states rest on small samples, so single figures are noisy.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 2.5 से 31.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 9.9 प्रतिशत है।

title: Secondary school dropout, UDISE+ 2024-25
takeaway: Secondary school dropout rate ranges from 2.0 per cent in Chandigarh to 20.0 per cent in West Bengal.
policy: Bihar is grey because the API reports exactly 0, which is not a credible measurement. A grey state here has no usable figure, not a low one.
title_hi: माध्यमिक स्तर पर स्कूल छोड़ना, UDISE+ 2024-25
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 2.0 से 20.0 प्रतिशत तक है।

title: Crimes against women recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Registered crimes against women run from 5.1 per lakh women in Nagaland to 130.7 in Delhi. The India figure is 64.6, from 66.2 in 2023.
policy: This counts registrations, not incidence. A higher figure can reflect easier reporting as well as more crime, so states should not be ranked on it.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच दर्ज महिला-विरोधी अपराध 5.1 से 130.7 प्रति लाख महिलाओं तक हैं। भारत का आँकड़ा 64.6 है, जो 2023 में 66.2 था।

title: Rape cases recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Registered rape cases run from 0.8 per lakh women in Ladakh to 16.6 in Chandigarh. The India figure is 4.3, from 4.4 in 2023.
policy: Rape of girls is mostly booked under the POCSO Act, so this map does not hold every rape case. A higher figure can reflect easier reporting as well as more crime, so states should not be ranked on it.
takeaway_hi: दर्ज बलात्कार के मामले लद्दाख में 0.8 से चंडीगढ़ में 16.6 प्रति लाख महिलाओं तक हैं। भारत का आँकड़ा 4.3 है, जो 2023 में 4.4 था।

title: Cruelty by husband or relatives, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Registered cruelty by a husband or his relatives runs from 0.4 per lakh women in Goa to 52.8 in Telangana. The India figure is 17.6, from 19.7 in 2023.
policy: This is a count of cases registered, and it is not the same as the spousal violence women report in surveys such as NFHS. A higher figure can reflect easier reporting as well as more crime, so states should not be ranked on it.
title_hi: पति या रिश्तेदारों द्वारा क्रूरता, NCRB 2024
takeaway_hi: पति या रिश्तेदारों द्वारा दर्ज क्रूरता गोवा में 0.4 से तेलंगाना में 52.8 प्रति लाख महिलाओं तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 17.6 है, जो 2023 में 19.7 था।

title: Dowry deaths recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Registered dowry deaths run from none registered in 11 states and territories to 1.78 per lakh women in Uttar Pradesh. The India figure is 0.84, from 0.91 in 2023.
policy: A zero here means none were registered, not that none occurred. A higher figure can reflect easier reporting as well as more crime, so states should not be ranked on it.
takeaway_hi: दर्ज दहेज मृत्यु 11 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में शून्य से उत्तर प्रदेश में 1.78 प्रति लाख महिलाओं तक हैं। भारत का आँकड़ा 0.84 है, जो 2023 में 0.91 था।

title: Acid attack cases recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Registered acid attacks reach 6.13 per crore women in both West Bengal and Manipur, against 1.73 for India (1.67 in 2023). Fifteen states and territories registered none.
policy: The counts are small, so one case moves a small state a long way. A higher figure can reflect easier reporting as well as more crime, so states should not be ranked on it.
title_hi: दर्ज एसिड हमले के मामले, NCRB 2024
takeaway_hi: दर्ज एसिड हमले पश्चिम बंगाल और मणिपुर, दोनों में 6.13 प्रति करोड़ महिलाओं तक हैं, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 1.73 है (2023 में 1.67)। 15 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।

title: Change in forest cover, 2021 to 2023
source: Forest Survey of India (ISFR 2023, via MoSPI)
takeaway: Forest cover rose by 156 sq km across India between 2021 and 2023, but states split. Mizoram gained 242 sq km and Gujarat 180, while Madhya Pradesh lost 372, Andhra Pradesh 139 and Telangana 100.
policy: Forest cover is satellite-measured tree canopy over one hectare, so plantations and orchards count, and a gain does not mean more natural forest. Puducherry and the merged Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu have no usable figure in the source, so they are grey.
takeaway_hi: ISFR 2021 और 2023 के बीच भारत में वन आच्छादन 156 वर्ग किमी बढ़ा, पर राज्यों में बँटवारा है। मिज़ोरम में 242 और गुजरात में 180 वर्ग किमी की बढ़त हुई, जबकि मध्य प्रदेश में 372, आंध्र प्रदेश में 139 और तेलंगाना में 100 वर्ग किमी की कमी आई।

title: Heat-wave days, 2022-24 average
takeaway: Heat-wave days run from 0.3 a summer in Assam to 17.0 in Punjab, with Haryana at 16.7 and Jharkhand at 15.7. Only 19 states report all three years.
policy: Single years swing widely (Uttarakhand reported 15, 0 and 22 days in 2022, 2023 and 2024), so this three-year average is still a rough guide. Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Kerala, Mizoram and Puducherry have missing years, and 12 other states and territories are not in the source at all.
takeaway_hi: लू वाले दिन असम में 0.3 प्रति गर्मी से पंजाब में 17.0 तक हैं, हरियाणा में 16.7 और झारखंड में 15.7 के साथ। केवल 19 राज्य तीनों वर्षों के आँकड़े देते हैं।

title: Pending cases per working judge, March 2026
source: NJDG and Nyaya Vikas (Lok Sabha, March 2026)
takeaway: A working judicial officer in Uttar Pradesh faces 4,563 pending cases, against 99 in Sikkim. The India figure is 2,359.
policy: The cases and the judges come from different sources and the judges table carries no date, so this is a rough guide. West Bengal and Andaman and Nicobar share one figure because the source merges their judges. Meghalaya is grey because its pendency row contradicts itself in the source. Pending cases mix old and new filings of every kind, so the ratio does not measure how fast a judge works.
title_hi: प्रति कार्यरत न्यायाधीश लंबित मामले, मार्च 2026
takeaway_hi: उत्तर प्रदेश में एक कार्यरत न्यायिक अधिकारी के सामने 4,563 लंबित मामले हैं, जबकि सिक्किम में 99। भारत का आँकड़ा 2,359 है।

title: Vacant judicial posts, subordinate courts, 2026
takeaway: Nearly one in five sanctioned posts in the subordinate judiciary is vacant (18.8 per cent), from none in Lakshadweep to 47.1 per cent in Ladakh and 42.4 in Meghalaya.
policy: Small territories swing on a few posts: Ladakh's 47.1 per cent is 8 of 17 posts. The source's own national vacancy total (4,868) does not match its state rows (4,880), so the India figure here is computed from the rows.
takeaway_hi: अधीनस्थ न्यायपालिका में लगभग हर पाँच में से एक स्वीकृत पद रिक्त है (18.8 प्रतिशत), लक्षद्वीप में शून्य से लद्दाख में 47.1 और मेघालय में 42.4 प्रतिशत तक।

title: Crimes against Scheduled Castes recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: Madhya Pradesh registered 68.5 cases per lakh Scheduled Caste people, Rajasthan 57.3 and Bihar 45.6, against 27.7 for India. West Bengal registered 0.5, with 116 cases among 214.6 lakh Scheduled Caste people, and Tripura none.
policy: The map counts registrations. A low figure can mean few atrocities or few that reach a police station and get recorded under the SC/ST Act, so a state with a very low rate has not shown that it is safer. Ten states and territories with under 1 lakh Scheduled Caste people are left grey because one case would swing their rate by more than 100.
title_hi: अनुसूचित जातियों के विरुद्ध दर्ज अपराध, NCRB 2024
takeaway_hi: मध्य प्रदेश में प्रति लाख अनुसूचित जाति व्यक्तियों पर 68.5 मामले दर्ज हुए, राजस्थान में 57.3 और बिहार में 45.6, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 27.7 है। पश्चिम बंगाल में 0.5 (214.6 लाख अनुसूचित जाति आबादी में 116 मामले) और त्रिपुरा में शून्य।

title: Honour killings recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: NCRB recorded 36 murders with honour killing as the motive in 2024. Bihar had the most (6), then Jharkhand and Punjab (5 each). Manipur has the highest rate, 3.07 per crore, from one case. Twenty-three states and territories recorded none.
policy: A zero means no murder was recorded under this motive, which is not the same as none occurring: a family that reports an honour killing as a suicide or an accident leaves no trace in this table. With counts this small the map is a list of where the motive was written down, and it should not be read as a ranking.
takeaway_hi: NCRB ने 2024 में ऑनर किलिंग को उद्देश्य बताकर 36 हत्याएँ दर्ज कीं। सबसे अधिक बिहार (6) में, फिर झारखंड और पंजाब (5-5) में। मणिपुर की दर सबसे ऊँची (प्रति करोड़ 3.07) है, जो एक ही मामले से बनी है। 23 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।

title: Murders linked to witchcraft recorded, NCRB 2024
takeaway: NCRB recorded 54 murders with witchcraft as the motive in 2024. Madhya Pradesh had the most (17), then Chhattisgarh (10) and Odisha (7). Nagaland has the highest rate, 4.42 per crore, from one case, and Chhattisgarh is next at 3.26 from ten. Twenty-five states and territories recorded none.
policy: The table counts murders only. Assaults, banishment and other harm done to people branded as witches are not in it, and a murder is recorded under this motive only if the police write it down. With counts this small, a single case moves a small state to the top.
title_hi: डायन-शिकार से जुड़ी दर्ज हत्याएँ, NCRB 2024
takeaway_hi: NCRB ने 2024 में डायन/जादू-टोने को उद्देश्य बताकर 54 हत्याएँ दर्ज कीं। सबसे अधिक मध्य प्रदेश (17) में, फिर छत्तीसगढ़ (10) और ओडिशा (7) में। नागालैंड की दर सबसे ऊँची (प्रति करोड़ 4.42) है, जो एक मामले से बनी है; छत्तीसगढ़ 3.26 पर दस मामलों से अगला है। 25 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।

title: GSDP per head, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway: Sikkim produces Rs 7,63,749 per person and Goa Rs 7,37,738, against Rs 76,374 in Bihar and Rs 1,26,304 in Uttar Pradesh. Eleven of the 32 states and territories with a figure are under Rs 2 lakh per person. Bihar grew 26 per cent in two years at current prices and Goa 36 per cent.
policy: Output per head counts what is produced inside a state, not what its residents earn or keep. Sikkim, Goa, Delhi and Chandigarh are small economies and city-states, so their figures say little about the average household. The 2024-25 figure is an estimate that states revise, and Nagaland and Ladakh have none for the year.
title_hi: प्रति व्यक्ति राज्य सकल घरेलू उत्पाद, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway_hi: सिक्किम में प्रति व्यक्ति 7,63,749 रुपये और गोवा में 7,37,738 रुपये का उत्पादन होता है, जबकि बिहार में 76,374 और उत्तर प्रदेश में 1,26,304। आँकड़े वाले 32 में से 11 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में यह 2 लाख रुपये से कम है।

title: Agriculture share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway: Agriculture is 41.3% of Madhya Pradesh's output and 38.0% of Tripura's, against 0.3% in Delhi and 0.5% in Chandigarh. The middle state is at 18.1%. Manipur's share fell most between 2022-23 and 2024-25, by 3.4 points.
policy: A share of output is not a share of jobs, and farm work employs a much larger share of workers than its share of output suggests. The share also falls when other sectors grow faster, so a lower number is not proof that farming did badly.
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में कृषि का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway_hi: मध्य प्रदेश के उत्पादन में कृषि का हिस्सा 41.3% और त्रिपुरा में 38.0% है, जबकि दिल्ली में 0.3% और चंडीगढ़ में 0.5%। बीच के राज्य में यह 18.1% है।

title: Manufacturing share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway: Manufacturing is 38.4% of Sikkim's output, 32.8% of Gujarat's and 27.8% of Goa's, but under 2% in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Mizoram. The middle state is at 11.4%. Gujarat's share fell 2.1 points in two years and Sikkim's rose 2.7.
policy: In a small economy one large unit can move the share a long way, so Sikkim's figure and the small shares in the north-east and the islands say as much about size as about policy.
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में विनिर्माण का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway_hi: सिक्किम के उत्पादन में विनिर्माण का हिस्सा 38.4%, गुजरात में 32.8% और गोवा में 27.8% है, जबकि अरुणाचल प्रदेश, मणिपुर और मिज़ोरम में 2% से कम। बीच के राज्य में 11.4%।

title: Services share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway: Services are 89.4% of Chandigarh's output and 86.1% of Delhi's, and 69.2% of Karnataka's. They are 35.5% in Madhya Pradesh, 32.3% in Chhattisgarh and 29.9% in Sikkim. The middle state is at 49.2%.
policy: Services here include public administration and real estate, which includes the imputed rent of owner-occupied homes, so a high share does not mean a state sells software or finance. Mining, electricity and construction are counted outside services.
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में सेवाओं का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25
takeaway_hi: सेवाएँ चंडीगढ़ के उत्पादन का 89.4%, दिल्ली का 86.1% और कर्नाटक का 69.2% हैं। मध्य प्रदेश में 35.5%, छत्तीसगढ़ में 32.3% और सिक्किम में 29.9%। बीच के राज्य में 49.2%।

title: Children with fever or ARI symptoms taken to a health facility, NFHS-6
takeaway: Nagaland takes 34.0 per cent of children with fever or breathing symptoms for care, Mizoram 42.2 and Assam 44.4, against 86.9 in Punjab and 80.3 in Karnataka. The India figure is 68.8 per cent, almost unchanged from 69.0 in NFHS-5. Punjab rose 29.6 points and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu fell 14.5.
policy: The figure counts children taken to any health provider, public or private, and says nothing about the quality of care. A figure for a small territory rests on few children, and Chandigarh's 92.1 is based on 25 to 49 cases, so it is flagged and the takeaway compares Punjab, the highest figure without that flag.
title_hi: बुखार या ARI लक्षण वाले बच्चे जिन्हें स्वास्थ्य केंद्र ले जाया गया, NFHS-6
takeaway_hi: नागालैंड में बुखार या साँस के लक्षण वाले 34.0 प्रतिशत बच्चों को इलाज के लिए ले जाया गया, मिज़ोरम में 42.2 और असम में 44.4, जबकि पंजाब में 86.9 और कर्नाटक में 80.3। भारत का आँकड़ा 68.8 प्रतिशत है, NFHS-5 के 69.0 से लगभग वही।

title: Private school enrolment share, UDISE+ 2024-25
takeaway: Private unaided schools enrol 67.5% of students in Nagaland, 62.7% in Manipur and 60.8% in Telangana, against 7.1% in West Bengal, 12.0% in Goa and 12.7% in Bihar. Across all states and territories the share is 36.8%, up from 31.9% in 2022-23, and it rose in every state and territory.
policy: Government-aided schools are privately managed but publicly funded and are not counted as private here, so a low share can mean a large aided sector rather than a large government one. The two-year rise is large and the source does not say how much of it is a change in the schools or in how they were counted.
title_hi: निजी स्कूलों में नामांकन का हिस्सा, UDISE+ 2024-25

title: Regular employees with no written contract, PLFS 2023-24
takeaway: In Punjab 84.5% of regular wage and salaried employees have no written contract, in Rajasthan 77.1% and in Gujarat 71.9%, against 10.0% in Arunachal Pradesh, 11.4% in Mizoram and 12.5% in Nagaland. The India figure is 58.0%, from 58.6% a year earlier. Bihar rose 10.1 points in the year.
policy: The measure covers only regular wage and salaried employees, who are a minority of workers. A high share in a state with much private-sector salaried work, and a low one where most salaried jobs are in government, partly reflect who the employers are. A written contract is not the same as social security cover.
title_hi: बिना लिखित अनुबंध वाले नियमित कर्मचारी, PLFS 2023-24
takeaway_hi: पंजाब में 84.5% नियमित वेतनभोगी कर्मचारियों के पास लिखित अनुबंध नहीं है, राजस्थान में 77.1% और गुजरात में 71.9%, जबकि अरुणाचल प्रदेश में 10.0%, मिज़ोरम में 11.4% और नागालैंड में 12.5%। भारत का आँकड़ा 58.0% है, जो एक साल पहले 58.6% था।
